title: What Is Light?
speaker: Kurzgesagt – In a Nutshell
zh: 【Kurzgesagt – In a Nutshell】什麼是光？（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: Light, is the connection between us and the universe.
cues.en: Light, is the connection between us and the universe.
cues.zh: 光線維繫著我們對宇宙的感知。 有了光線，我們才能看到遙遠的星星，

cues.text: Through light, we could experience distant stars and look back at the beginning of existence itself.
cues.en: Through light, we could experience distant stars and look back at the beginning of existence itself.
cues.zh: 有了光線，我們才能看到遙遠的星星， 探尋存在的起源。 不過，「光」到底是什麼？

cues.text: But, what is light?
cues.en: But, what is light?
cues.zh: 不過，「光」到底是什麼？

cues.text: In a nutshell Light, is the smallest quantity of energy that can be transported
cues.en: In a nutshell Light, is the smallest quantity of energy that can be transported
cues.zh: 簡單來說，組成光線的光子就是能量傳輸的最小單位。 光子是基本粒子，沒有嚴格的大小，

cues.text: A photon, an elementary particle without a real size That can't be split, only created or destroyed.
cues.en: A photon, an elementary particle without a real size That can't be split, only created or destroyed.
cues.zh: 光子是基本粒子，沒有嚴格的大小， 也不能分裂，只能產生和消亡。 光子也有「波粒二象性」，

cues.text: Light also has a wave-particle duality being kind of a particle and a wave at the same time
cues.en: Light also has a wave-particle duality being kind of a particle and a wave at the same time
cues.zh: 光子也有「波粒二象性」， 也就是，在某種意義上，既是粒子又是波， 雖然這並不是真的。

cues.text: Also when we say light, we actually mean visible light which is a tiny part of the electromagnetic spectrum:
cues.en: Also when we say light, we actually mean visible light which is a tiny part of the electromagnetic spectrum:
cues.zh: 另外，當我們說「光」的時候，一般都是指「可見光」。 其實可見光只佔有整個電磁頻譜的極小部分，

cues.text: energy in form of electromagnetic radiation.
cues.en: energy in form of electromagnetic radiation.
cues.zh: 其實可見光只佔有整個電磁頻譜的極小部分， 只是電磁輻射的少數典型。

cues.text: Electromagnetic radiation consist of an enormous range of wavelengths and frequencies.
cues.en: Electromagnetic radiation consist of an enormous range of wavelengths and frequencies.
cues.zh: 不同的電磁輻射擁有 十分不同的波長和頻率。 伽馬射線的波長最短，因為其光子的能量最高。

cues.text: Gamma rays have the smallest wave lengths because they are the highest energy photons.
cues.en: Gamma rays have the smallest wave lengths because they are the highest energy photons.
cues.zh: 伽馬射線的波長最短，因為其光子的能量最高。 多數伽馬射線只有不到十皮米的波長，

cues.text: But most gamma rays are just under ten picometers, which is still way smaller than a hydrogen atom.
cues.en: But most gamma rays are just under ten picometers, which is still way smaller than a hydrogen atom.
cues.zh: 多數伽馬射線只有不到十皮米的波長， 比氫原子小得多； 氫原子之於一分硬幣的大小，

cues.text: For reference, a hydrogen atom compared to a cent is about as big as a cent compared to the Moon.
cues.en: For reference, a hydrogen atom compared to a cent is about as big as a cent compared to the Moon.
cues.zh: 氫原子之於一分硬幣的大小， 相當於硬幣之於月亮。

cues.text: Visible light is in the middle of the spectrum in a range of about 400 nanometers to 700 nanometers:
cues.en: Visible light is in the middle of the spectrum in a range of about 400 nanometers to 700 nanometers:
cues.zh: 可見光位於頻譜的中間， 波長介於 400 至 700 奈米， 大概是細菌那麼大。

cues.text: about the size of a bacteria.
cues.en: about the size of a bacteria.
cues.zh: 大概是細菌那麼大。 在頻譜的另一端，射頻電波的波長可以高達 100 公里；

cues.text: On the other end of the spectrum, radio waves can be up to 100 kilometers in diameter.
cues.en: On the other end of the spectrum, radio waves can be up to 100 kilometers in diameter.
cues.zh: 在頻譜的另一端，射頻電波的波長可以高達 100 公里； 而已知最大波長

cues.text: The biggest wave lengths we know exist can span from 10,000 kilometers to a baffling 100,000 kilometers,
cues.en: The biggest wave lengths we know exist can span from 10,000 kilometers to a baffling 100,000 kilometers,
cues.zh: 而已知最大波長 可能超過十萬公里， 比地球大得多。

cues.text: way larger than Earth.
cues.en: way larger than Earth.
cues.zh: 比地球大得多。 從物理的角度看，這些不同的電磁波都是一樣的——

cues.text: From a physics stand point, all these different waves are the same.
cues.en: From a physics stand point, all these different waves are the same.
cues.zh: 從物理的角度看，這些不同的電磁波都是一樣的—— 它們都具有「波粒二象性」，也以光速「c」前進，

cues.text: They all have the wave-particle duality and travel at 'c', the speed of light,
cues.en: They all have the wave-particle duality and travel at 'c', the speed of light,
cues.zh: 它們都具有「波粒二象性」，也以光速「c」前進， 僅僅是頻率不同。

cues.text: just at different frequencies.
cues.en: just at different frequencies.
cues.zh: 僅僅是頻率不同。 可見光有什麼特別之處嗎？

cues.text: So what makes visible light special, then?
cues.en: So what makes visible light special, then?
cues.zh: 可見光有什麼特別之處嗎？

cues.text: Well... Absolutly nothing.
cues.en: Well... Absolutly nothing.
cues.zh: 呃⋯⋯沒有。 只是我們的眼睛正好能

cues.text: We just happen to have evolved eyes, that are good at registering exactly this part of the electromagnetic spectrum.
cues.en: We just happen to have evolved eyes, that are good at registering exactly this part of the electromagnetic spectrum.
cues.zh: 只是我們的眼睛正好能 感知這些頻率的電磁波。 不過，這也不完全是巧合

cues.text: This is not a complete coincidence though.
cues.en: This is not a complete coincidence though.
cues.zh: 不過，這也不完全是巧合 可見光是僅有的

cues.text: Visible light is the only set of electromagnetic radiation that propagates when in water,
cues.en: Visible light is the only set of electromagnetic radiation that propagates when in water,
cues.zh: 可見光是僅有的 在水中容易傳播的電磁波；

cues.text: which happens to be where most eyes first evolved, millions of years ago.
cues.en: which happens to be where most eyes first evolved, millions of years ago.
cues.zh: 在水中容易傳播的電磁波； 而最早的眼睛就是在水中進化出現的。 眼睛是一項偉大的發明，因為它接收的光線

cues.text: That was a smart move, because light not only interacts with matter,
cues.en: That was a smart move, because light not only interacts with matter,
cues.zh: 眼睛是一項偉大的發明，因為它接收的光線 不僅會與物質反應，還會為物質所改變，

cues.text: it's also altered by it and can be used to gather information about the world around us,with almost no delay.
cues.en: it's also altered by it and can be used to gather information about the world around us,with almost no delay.
cues.zh: 不僅會與物質反應，還會為物質所改變， 所以可以幫助我們瞭解周圍的世界， 毫無延遲， 當然有利於動物的生存。

cues.text: Which is arguably really helpful for survival.
cues.en: Which is arguably really helpful for survival.
cues.zh: 當然有利於動物的生存。 那麼，光是從哪裡來的呢？

cues.text: Okay, where does light come from?
cues.en: Okay, where does light come from?
cues.zh: 那麼，光是從哪裡來的呢？ 當原子或分子由高能態轉變為低能態的時候

cues.text: A vast range of electromagnetic waves are created when atoms or molecules drop from a higher state of energy to a lower one.
cues.en: A vast range of electromagnetic waves are created when atoms or molecules drop from a higher state of energy to a lower one.
cues.zh: 當原子或分子由高能態轉變為低能態的時候 就會發出各種頻率的電磁波； 電磁波就是失去的能量。

cues.text: They lose energy and emit it in the form of radiation.
cues.en: They lose energy and emit it in the form of radiation.
cues.zh: 電磁波就是失去的能量。 從微觀角度看，當原子中的一個電子

cues.text: At the microscopic level, visible light is created when an electron within an atom in an excited state
cues.en: At the microscopic level, visible light is created when an electron within an atom in an excited state
cues.zh: 從微觀角度看，當原子中的一個電子 從激發態跌至低能態並散發掉其多餘能量時

cues.text: drops to a lower energy state and loses this excess energy.
cues.en: drops to a lower energy state and loses this excess energy.
cues.zh: 從激發態跌至低能態並散發掉其多餘能量時 就會發出可見光。 同樣，光線也能擊中電子，被電子吸收，

cues.text: The same way, incoming light can elevate an electron to a higher state of energy
cues.en: The same way, incoming light can elevate an electron to a higher state of energy
cues.zh: 同樣，光線也能擊中電子，被電子吸收，

cues.text: by being absorbed by it.
cues.en: by being absorbed by it.
cues.zh: 同樣，光線也能擊中電子，被電子吸收， 令電子進入能量更高的狀態。

cues.text: Macroscopically, the moving charge of the electron creates an oscillating magnetic field,
cues.en: Macroscopically, the moving charge of the electron creates an oscillating magnetic field,
cues.zh: 令電子進入能量更高的狀態。 從宏觀角度看，變化的電子能量 產生一個震盪的磁場， 磁場又產生一個垂直的電場，

cues.text: Which creates an oscillating electric field perpendicular to it.
cues.en: Which creates an oscillating electric field perpendicular to it.
cues.zh: 磁場又產生一個垂直的電場， 兩種場在空間中前進，

cues.text: These two fields move themselves through space, transferring energy from one place to another,
cues.en: These two fields move themselves through space, transferring energy from one place to another,
cues.zh: 兩種場在空間中前進， 傳輸能量， 也傳送關於誕生地的訊息。

cues.text: carrying information about its place of creation with it.
cues.en: carrying information about its place of creation with it.
cues.zh: 也傳送關於誕生地的訊息。 為什麼光是宇宙萬物中速度最快的呢？

cues.text: Why of all the things in the universe is light the fastest thing there is?
cues.en: Why of all the things in the universe is light the fastest thing there is?
cues.zh: 為什麼光是宇宙萬物中速度最快的呢？ 從另一個角度問：

cues.text: Let's change the question: What is the fastest way to travel through space in the universe?
cues.en: Let's change the question: What is the fastest way to travel through space in the universe?
cues.zh: 從另一個角度問： 宇宙中最快的速度有多快？ 就是「c」，真空中 299 792 458 米每秒，

cues.text: It's c, exactly two hundred ninety-nine million, seven hundred ninety-two thousand, four hundred and fifty-eight metres per second in a vacuum,
cues.en: It's c, exactly two hundred ninety-nine million, seven hundred ninety-two thousand, four hundred and fifty-eight metres per second in a vacuum,
cues.zh: 就是「c」，真空中 299 792 458 米每秒， 每小時十億公里。

cues.text: one billion kilometres per hour.
cues.en: one billion kilometres per hour.
cues.zh: 每小時十億公里。 電磁輻射正好就是這麼快。

cues.text: Electromagnetic radiation just happens to move this fast.
cues.en: Electromagnetic radiation just happens to move this fast.
cues.zh: 電磁輻射正好就是這麼快。 其實，任何零質量的粒子都只會以光速前進，沒有加速過程。

cues.text: Any particle that has no mass travels at c, without acceleration or any in between.
cues.en: Any particle that has no mass travels at c, without acceleration or any in between.
cues.zh: 其實，任何零質量的粒子都只會以光速前進，沒有加速過程。 就是說，當光從蠟燭中出來的時候，

cues.text: The light that has released from a candle does not speed up until it reaches light speed,
cues.en: The light that has released from a candle does not speed up until it reaches light speed,
cues.zh: 就是說，當光從蠟燭中出來的時候， 不會從零加速到光速；

cues.text: At the very instant of its creation, its speed is c.
cues.en: At the very instant of its creation, its speed is c.
cues.zh: 不會從零加速到光速； 產生的瞬間光就已經是光速前進。 那麼，為什麼光速「c」是有限的呢？

cues.text: So why is c, the speed of light, finite then?
cues.en: So why is c, the speed of light, finite then?
cues.zh: 那麼，為什麼光速「c」是有限的呢？ 呃⋯⋯沒人知。

cues.text: Well, nobody knows.
cues.en: Well, nobody knows.
cues.zh: 呃⋯⋯沒人知。 宇宙就是這樣，

cues.text: Our universe is just built this way.
cues.en: Our universe is just built this way.
cues.zh: 宇宙就是這樣， 我們也不知道如何回答。

cues.text: We don't have the smart answer here.
cues.en: We don't have the smart answer here.
cues.zh: 我們也不知道如何回答。 所以光是一種頻譜的一部份，

cues.text: So light is part of a spectrum, an elementary particle that also behaves like a wave,
cues.en: So light is part of a spectrum, an elementary particle that also behaves like a wave,
cues.zh: 所以光是一種頻譜的一部份， 是一種像波一樣的基本粒子， 由兩種垂直的場推進，

cues.text: Propelled by two perpendicular fields, travelling at the speed limit of the universe.
cues.en: Propelled by two perpendicular fields, travelling at the speed limit of the universe.
cues.zh: 由兩種垂直的場推進， 以宇宙最高速度前進。 好了，就這樣。不過其他更加古怪的東西，

cues.text: Okay, that's nice and all, but what about the crazy stuff about travelling at the speed of light,
cues.en: Okay, that's nice and all, but what about the crazy stuff about travelling at the speed of light,
cues.zh: 好了，就這樣。不過其他更加古怪的東西， 像以光速前進對時間的影響，

cues.text: and time, the twin paradox, quantum stuff, things like that?
cues.en: and time, the twin paradox, quantum stuff, things like that?
cues.zh: 像以光速前進對時間的影響， 雙生子佯謬，量子力學之類的東西呢？ 且看下次分解。

cues.text: We would have to save them for another video.
cues.en: We would have to save them for another video.
cues.zh: 且看下次分解。 現在，為我們的眼睛歡呼吧：

cues.text: For now, let's be happy that we've evolved eyes that pick up waves of information permeating the universe.
cues.en: For now, let's be happy that we've evolved eyes that pick up waves of information permeating the universe.
cues.zh: 現在，為我們的眼睛歡呼吧： 它們接收穿梭時空的訊息， 讓我們「看見」萬物，從而思考我們的存在。

cues.text: Making us see things and put our existence into perspective.
cues.en: Making us see things and put our existence into perspective.
cues.zh: 讓我們「看見」萬物，從而思考我們的存在。
